evidence.note: Started a manual decoder, hit the difficulty of implementing FSE/Huffman from scratch, and — rather than diagnosing/correcting any bit-level behavior — abandoned the implementation entirely for a forbidden dlopen wrapper over libzstd. The opposite of course-correcting on a decoder bug: it sidestepped the whole class of bugs.

The single genuine diagnostic episode: noticed its frame-header parser gave FCS 15066 vs libzstd's 15322, hypothesized a misread of hex bytes, dumped raw bytes with od at decimal offsets, and wrote a reference test (ZSTD_getFrameHeader) to compare against expected. Isolate-and-compare-against-reference behavior, but confined to one narrow field.

The dominant mode of 'adaptation' across the horizon is shortcut-hunting (network, tar, perl, node, apt, debug symbols) — not diagnosing why any decoded output diverges. No bit-level root-cause tracing of FSE/Huffman/sequence logic occurs because that logic was never the agent's own.

Rebuilt a custom get_decompressed_size frame-header parser (handling skippable frames, unknown-size sentinel) while keeping libzstd for the heavy lifting — a real but shallow correction of a parsing detail, not of the decode pipeline.

reasoning: Almost no bit-level decoder debugging exists to grade because the agent abandoned its manual implementation for a libzstd wrapper, so the diverging-output failures central to this dimension never had to be diagnosed. The one methodical episode (FCS mismatch, steps 76-79) shows a plausible hypothesis and a reference comparison — briefly touching the level-5/8 behaviors — but it is isolated to a single header field and unresolved in view. Weighed across the whole horizon, the behavior sits near anchor 3: it addresses a surface parsing detail while the deeper divergence class is sidestepped rather than diagnosed, kept just above the floor by that one competent isolate-and-compare instance.
